steps.tx: Irreversible fibro-inflammatory destruction of pancreatic parenchyma culminating in progressive exocrine and endocrine insufficiency characterizes **chronic pancreatitis**. In adult populations, chronic alcohol abuse represents the predisposing aetiological factor in over seventy percent of cases, alongside idiopathic, hereditary, and autoimmune pancreatitis. Patients suffer from intractable, disabling epigastric pain that characteristically bores through to the back, driving narcotics dependence and severe malnourishment.
steps.say: Chronic pancreatitis involves irreversible parenchymal fibrosis and ductal damage, presenting with disabling epigastric pain boring through to the back.

vis.alt: Gross and microscopic pathological diagram of chronic pancreatitis showing parenchymal fibrosis, ductal dilatation, and intraductal calculi.
vis.caption: Chronic pancreatitis: severe parenchymal fibrosis, calcified stones, and chain-of-lakes ductal dilatation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The principal goal of operative management in chronic pancreatitis is durable relief of intractable pain that has proven refractory to conservative medical and endoscopic therapy. Secondary indications for surgery include biliary obstruction from fibrous common duct encasement, duodenal stenosis, persistent symptomatic pseudocysts, or clinical inability to exclude pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Ductal morphology dictates the selection between decompressive, resective, or **hybrid procedures**.
steps.say: Surgery for chronic pancreatitis aims to relieve intractable pain and resolve biliary or duodenal compression when medical therapies fail.

rows: Dilated main duct (> 6-7 mm), normal head
Inflammatory head mass with dilated duct
Severe disease confined to head or tail

steps.tx: When a dilated pancreatic duct is the pain generator, the operation opens it like a book. The **Puestow procedure** lays the duct open along its length and sews a loop of jejunum over the gutter, letting stones and strictured juice drain sideways into bowel. It suits big duct disease, conventionally above seven millimetres, where endoscopic drainage has failed or the duct is packed with calculi. Resecting the head would overshoot such anatomy, so this decompressive classic survives every fashion for more radical surgery.
steps.say: The Puestow procedure drains a dilated pancreatic duct sideways into jejunum for big duct chronic pancreatitis.

steps.tx: When cross-sectional imaging reveals a markedly dilated main pancreatic duct exceeding six to seven millimetres with alternating strictures and calculi, termed chain-of-lakes, longitudinal surgical drainage is indicated. The benchmark historical operation is the **Puestow procedure**, formally modified by Partington and Rochelle. The main pancreatic duct is filleted open longitudinally from the neck to within one centimetre of the tail, calculi are cleared, and a Roux-en-Y jejuno-pancreatic anastomosis is constructed.
steps.say: The Puestow procedure fillets open the dilated pancreatic duct longitudinally and anastomoses it to a Roux-en-Y jejunal loop.

vis.alt: Anatomical schematic showing longitudinal filleting of the main pancreatic duct and Roux-en-Y side-to-side pancreaticojejunostomy.
vis.caption: Longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy: wide drainage of the dilated main pancreatic duct using a Roux-en-Y jejunal loop. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The modern Partington-Rochelle modification of the Puestow operation simplifies the technique by omitting splenectomy and distal pancreatectomy. By opening the duct along its anterior surface and creating an extensive side-to-side anastomosis, ductal hypertension is permanently relieved. However, long-term pain relief fails in over thirty percent of patients if an underlying inflammatory fibrotic mass residing in the **pancreatic head** is neglected.
steps.say: The Partington-Rochelle modification avoids splenectomy, but pain can recur if an inflammatory head mass is left unaddressed.

right.title: Partington-Rochelle
points: Current international standard for large ducts

steps.tx: To simultaneously decompress the dilated duct and excise the pacemaker of pain located within the pancreatic head, Charles Frey pioneered the **Frey procedure**. This ingenious hybrid technique combines longitudinal ductal unroofing with local core excision of the head of the pancreas. The anterior shell of the pancreatic head is cored out, preserving a thin rim of tissue along the duodenal curve and uncinate process.
steps.say: The Frey procedure cores out the fibrotic pancreatic head while unroofing the dilated duct, combining resection with longitudinal drainage.

nodes.label: Inflammatory Head Mass with Dilated Pancreatic Duct
Local Coring Resection of Pancreatic Head Parenchyma
Longitudinal Anterior Unroofing of Main Pancreatic Duct

steps.tx: A related duodenum-preserving resection of the pancreatic head is the Beger procedure. In the Beger operation, the pancreatic neck is formally transected over the portal vein and superior mesenteric vein, and the head of the pancreas is subcompletely excised, leaving only a small rim of tissue along the duodenum. Because it requires vascular dissection over the **portal vein**, the Beger procedure carries higher technical complexity than the Frey operation.
steps.say: The Beger procedure transects the pancreatic neck over mesenteric vessels to perform subtotal head excision while preserving the duodenum.

steps.tx: In patients with severe disease confined strictly to the pancreatic head where high suspicion of occult malignancy exists, classic or pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy remains the definitive intervention. Conversely, when chronic inflammation, stones, and strictures are limited entirely to the body and tail with a normal pancreatic head, spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy provides complete symptom resolution while minimizing the risk of post-splenectomy **systemic sepsis**.
steps.say: Suspected cancer in the head warrants a Whipple procedure, whereas isolated tail disease is managed with distal pancreatectomy.

left.title: Suspected Head Malignancy
points: Excision of head, duodenum, and bile duct

right.title: Isolated Distal Disease
points: Low risk of postoperative pancreatic fistula

steps.tx: Management of small-duct disease where the main pancreatic duct measures under three millimetres presents a major clinical challenge, as decompressive drainage is impossible. For these patients without an inflammatory head mass, bilateral thoracoscopic **splanchnicectomy** or computed tomography-guided celiac plexus neurolysis can interrupt visceral pain pathways. Splanchnicectomy achieves significant short-to-medium term pain reduction without accelerating parenchymal exocrine or endocrine loss.
steps.say: Small-duct chronic pancreatitis unsuitable for drainage is managed by thoracoscopic splanchnicectomy or celiac plexus neurolysis.
